# dsh-opencode-client

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that acts as an
**OpenCode client**: it connects to one or more remote `op

encode serve` instances and exposes their
projects, sessions and messages to dsh, delegates tasks in

to them, and registers OpenCode as a
native dsh subagent backend.

> OpenCode's own architecture: `opencode serve` exposes an OpenAPI HTTP server "that an opencode
> c

lient can use"; the TUI/web/SDK are clients. This plugin is another client, hosted in dsh.
>
> **Pri

mary role**: register OpenCode as a native dsh subagent backend
> (`opencode_subagent_<server>`) and

expose remote sessions/workspace as tools
> (`opencode_subagent`, `opencode_prompt`, shell/git/read

/find, catalogs). The embedded
> OpenCode Web UI (left/side panels) is an optional convenience for f

ull-fidelity work,
> not a replacement for the OpenCode client.
## Features

- **Server configuration** — `servers: [{ id, label?, url, password?, directory? }]`
- **Discovery**

— `GET /api/opencode-client/list` (server health, projects, sessions grouped by directory)
- **Sess

ion listing** — tool `opencode_sessions` + `GET /api/opencode-client/sessions`
- **Session messages*

* — tool `opencode_messages` + `GET /api/opencode-client/messages`
- **Agent catalog** — tool `openc

ode_agents` + `GET /api/opencode-client/agents` (primary/subagent, native/custom)
- **Delegation** —
tool `opencode_subagent` (new session, or continue with `session=`; optional `agent`, `model` and p

rompt-enforced `schema`); uses `prompt_async` + message polling with a blocking-prompt fallback
- **
Session info** — tool `opencode_session_info` (title/summary/todos/diff) and `opencode_share` (share

/unshare link)
- **Catalogs** — `opencode_models` (providers/models, credentials stripped), `opencod

e_commands`, `opencode_skills`, `opencode_tools`, `opencode_references`
- **Command execution** — `o

pencode_command` runs a remote command (e.g. `init`) inside a session
- **Workspace ops** — `opencod

e_shell`, `opencode_git_status`, `opencode_git_diff`, `opencode_read_file`, `opencode_find`
- **Sess
ion management** — `opencode_fork`, `opencode_children`, `opencode_summarize` (mutating), `opencode_

init` (writes AGENTS.md, requires confirm=true)
- **Turn-by-turn continuation** — `opencode_prompt`
sends one message to an existing remote session (fire-and-forget by default, `wait=true` to block);
read the reply with `opencode_messages`/`opencode_progress` and send the next message. This keeps a

remote worker session alive across dsh turns.
- **Live progress** — `opencode_progress` (current too

l/step, elapsed, output tail) fed by SSE tool events; delegation completes on the SSE idle event
- *
*Search & diagnostics** — `opencode_search` (v2 session search), `opencode_mcp` (MCP server status)
- **Attachments** — `opencode_subagent` accepts a `files` JSON array (text/base64 → data URL file pa

rts)
- **Abort** — `opencode_abort` stops a running remote session; a waiting delegation returns an

abort error instead of hanging.

## Subagent seam

The native `opencode_subagent_<server>` tools plug into dsh's `ctx.subagents` provider seam.
See doc

s/subagent-seam.md for the contract, our capability
mapping, and the applied optimizations (parent-a

gent attribution, event-driven wait,
idempotent dispose). Both `opencode_subagent` and the native pr

ovider share one
session-run lifecycle (`lib/session-run.js`): same session creation, interaction
tr

acking, async prompt + SSE idle wait and abort handling. Native subagent sessions are
titled `dsh su

bagent: <label>` so they are identifiable in the plugin page (which now
also shows session ids and t
he active tool of running servers).
## Documentation

- ARCHITECTURE.md — module map, data flows, design decisions
- COMPATIBILITY.md — dsh / OpenCode com

patibility and versioning policy
- docs/subagent-seam.md — dsh subagent provider contract
- docs/cha

t-ui-proposal.md — in-page remote-session chat proposal
- README.zh.md · TODO.md · CHANGELOG.md
## Compatibility & versioning

See COMPATIBILITY.md. The plugin follows independent semantic versioning, is
verified against dsh `0

.2.1-rc.2` and OpenCode `1.18.10/1.18.31/1.18.33`, and is not published to
npm for now (install from
git or a local path).
## Notes

- The remote OpenCode server must be reachable from the dsh host; `opencode serve` binds
`127.0.0.1`

by default — bind `0.0.0.0` or put it behind an SSH tunnel.
- Session continuation is done through

the OpenCode HTTP API; native external subagents still
execute once (matching Codex/Claude Code back

ends).
- Interactive questions asked by the remote agent are forwarded to dsh's user-question UI whe

n the
run was started by `opencode_subagent` (an agent is in scope); otherwise they are rejected.
-

**Structured output is prompt-enforced, not `format=`-enforced**: opencode 1.18.x has an upstream
bu

g — after a prompt carrying `format: {type:"json_schema"}`, it persists a `retryCount` field
that ma

kes `GET /session/{id}/message` return 400 (BadRequest), poisoning the session. The plugin
therefore

appends a "return only JSON matching this schema" instruction and validates the result
locally (`sc

hema` parameter), leaving the session readable.
- **Permission cards need a tool-initiated run**: ap

proval bridging uses the calling agent; a
delegation started over the HTTP endpoint (no agent in sco

pe) falls back to `allow`/`reject`.
- **Multiple servers** are configured as an array and aggregated

by the client (opencode itself has
no server-side federation).
- Permission/question requests are a

nswered while a delegated run is active: SSE events are handled
immediately, with a 15s polling fall

back when the stream is unavailable.
- The plugin page shows `live` (SSE connected) and the number o
f currently running sessions.
